chunks: Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā and Muḥammad ibn Sahl, from their shaykhs, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If an important need arises for you before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then fast for three consecutive days: Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. Then when Friday comes, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills, perform ghusl, wear a new garment, then go up to the highest place in your house, pray two rakʿahs there, raise your hands to the sky, then say:

O Allah, I have come into Your precinct by my recognition of Your oneness and Your absolute self-sufficiency, and that none has power over my need except You. And I have known, my Lord, that whenever Your blessing becomes manifest upon me, my need of You intensifies. A worry of such-and-such has come upon me, and You know how to remove it, without being taught, vast without strain. So I ask You by Your Name which You placed upon the mountains and they were blasted away, and You placed it upon the heaven and it split apart, and upon the stars and they scattered, and upon the earth and it was spread out. And I ask You by the truth which You placed with Muḥammad and the Imams عليهم السلام—and you name them to the last of them—that You send blessings upon Muḥammad and his Ahl al-Bayt, fulfill my need, make its difficulty easy for me, and suffice me regarding its burden. If You do so, then to You belongs all praise; and if You do not do so, then to You belongs all praise, while I do not hold You unjust in Your judgment, nor suspect in Your decree, nor unfair in Your justice.

And place your cheek upon the ground and say: O Allah, indeed Yūnus ibn Mattā, Your servant, called upon You in the belly of the whale, and he was Your servant, so You answered him; and I am Your servant calling upon You, so answer me.
Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Often I would have a need, and I would supplicate with this supplication, then return having had it fulfilled.

key_terms.حَاجَةٌ: an important need or request sought from Allah
key_terms.ٱلْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams عليهم السلام, invoked here in connection with the supplication

ai.seo_question: What supplication and devotional practice is recommended for fulfilling an important need according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a prescribed salat al-hajah practice that combines fasting, ghusl, prayer, and a specific du'a for urgent needs. It emphasizes tawhid, reliance upon Allah, invocation through the truth of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the Imams عليهم السلام, and contentment with the divine decree while seeking relief.
